title: Trading Policy (Schedule 9)

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the entity's activities, including any Director (executive or otherwise); the Company has determined this to be its Directors and those employees directly reporting to the Managing Director.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman; distinguished only for approval purposes, obtaining prior approval directly from the Board rather than from the Chairman.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents or other associates through whom Key Management Personnel deal, such as family members, family trusts and family companies.

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's Annual Financial Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after the release of the Company's Annual Financial Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Half Year Financial Report of the Company
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after the release of the Half Year Financial Report of the Company

windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after the release of the Company's quarterly reports (if applicable)

rules.detail: Derivatives are not mentioned anywhere in the policy; the policy regulates only buying, selling and exercising rights in the Company's securities.
Hedging is not mentioned or defined anywhere in the policy.
No mention of monetisation, forward sales or similar structures.
Short selling is not named, but any sale of Company securities requires prior written approval of the Chairman or Board under the general approval regime.
rules.evidence: Any Key Management Personnel (other than the Chairman) wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman or the Board before doing so.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
CFDs and other derivative instruments are not named or otherwise addressed.

Margin lending arrangements are not directly regulated; entering one is not a 'buy, sell or exercise' of securities so does not trigger the section 5.1 approval regime, and the policy expressly contemplates such arrangements by exempting a lender's later forced sale from Closed Period restrictions and confirming it would not breach insider trading laws.
rules.evidence: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage or charge over Company securities is not one of the regulated activities (buy, sell, exercise) and is expressly contemplated: 'a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws'.
rules.evidence: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: Secured financing generally (not limited to margin loans) is implicitly permitted on the same basis as margin lending and mortgages/charges, with no approval step named for entering the arrangement itself.
rules.evidence: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: No defined holding period; aspirational 'should never' language, with a carve-out for selling shares shortly after option exercise.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: Any Key Management Personnel (other than the Chairman) wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman or the Board before doing so.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: If the Chairman wishes to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities, the Chairman must obtain the prior approval of the Board before doing so.

carve_outs: exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter
short_term.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

exceptions.evidence: acquire ordinary shares in the Company by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to ordinary shares
acquire Company securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class
acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders or securities of the same class
acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise options under an employee incentive scheme (as that term is defined in the ASX Listing Rules)
withdraw ordinary shares in the Company held on behalf of the Key Management Personnel in an employee incentive scheme ... where the withdrawal is permitted by the rules of that scheme
acquire ordinary shares in the Company as a result of the exercise of options held under an employee option scheme
transfer securities of the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the restricted person is a beneficiary

make an investment in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a restricted person is a trustee, trade in the securities of the Company by that trust, provided the restricted person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer

trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back
dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

exercise (but not sell securities following exercise) an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or convert a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a prohibited period
trade under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy

Key Management Personnel who are not in possession of inside information ... may be given prior written clearance by the Board to sell or otherwise dispose of Company securities in a Closed Period where the person is in severe financial hardship

Exceptional circumstances may apply to the disposal of Company securities by a Key Management Personnel if the person is required by a court order, a court enforceable undertaking for example in a bona fide family settlement, to transfer or sell securities of the Company

financing_disclosure: Key Management Personnel; forced sale of Company securities by a secured lender (a sale of securities); to the Company Secretary in writing; within 2 business days of the transaction occurring

exemption_authority: The Board may exempt a Closed Period sale for severe financial hardship (a pressing financial commitment satisfiable only by selling) or exceptional circumstances (court order, court-enforceable undertaking, or other overriding legal/regulatory requirement), determined case-by-case on written application with supporting documentation; any exemption is in writing and specifies the time period for the sale. The Board may also vary (relax) a Closed Period generally by announcement to all KMP.

bespoke_clauses.topic: granting security is not a regulated 'dealing'
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because the approval regime in section 5.1 is confined to 'buy, sell or exercise rights', granting security over shares to secure the collar's loan appears to fall outside the clearance requirement entirely, and a subsequent forced sale on default is expressly carved out of both the Closed Period ban and insider trading exposure.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale exemption applies 'at any time'
bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel may at any time: ... dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale under the loan secured on the collared shares can proceed even during a Closed Period, without needing an exceptional-circumstances application.

bespoke_clauses.clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collared shares originate from option exercise, a cashless-exercise sale to fund the strike price must occur outside Closed Periods, which can affect the timing of when shares become available to post as collateral.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to both the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company and its subsidiaries on issue from time to time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy has no express hedging, derivatives, CFD or short-selling regime, so the OTC put and call legs of a collar are not clearly 'securities' dealings requiring approval under this document, though ordinary insider trading law still applies to their execution.

summary: A funded collar appears achievable, though largely because this policy is narrowly drafted and simply silent on derivatives, hedging and secured financing rather than expressly permitting them. The approval regime in section 5.1 only catches 'buy, sell or exercise rights' in Company securities, so granting security over shares to a bank, and the OTC put/call legs themselves, are not clearly caught by the clearance procedure at all; a lender's forced sale on default is expressly exempted from Closed Periods and confirmed not to breach insider trading law. Ordinary share sales and purchases still require prior written Board or Chairman approval, must avoid the Annual/Half-Year/quarterly Closed Periods (two weeks before to 48 hours after results), and must be notified to the Company Secretary within two business days. Because the policy predates modern hedging/derivative-specific drafting, a bank should treat the absence of an express prohibition as a gap rather than a clear permission, and confirm with the company's legal advisers (as section 5.4 requires for any KMP sale) before structuring the collar and loan. No minimum shareholding requirement, vesting-based restriction, or short-term holding period is specified beyond a general, undefined discouragement of short-term trading.
